description.narrative: Stöd till utveckling av Liberias handelspolitiska kapacitet, genom samarbete mellan Kommerskollegium i Sverige och Handels- och Industriministeriet i Liberia.
Support to development of Liberian trade-policy capacity, through co-operation between Swedish Board of National Trade and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry in Liberia.

The initial objective of the NBT support was to facilitate Liberia’s WTO accession during 2013-2017. In 2015, the Embassy of Sweden, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI) and Swedish National Board of Trade (NBT) agreed to revise the project objective to support Liberia to take advantage of its WTO membership.

This contribution was designed with the primary objective of providing technical and operational assistance to Liberia in order to support the country in becoming a member of WTO. By 2016, this objective had been fully met as Liberia acceded to the WTO and the country’s Legislature had ratified the WTO accession instrument, making Liberia a WTO member. After Libera’s WTO membership was achieved, a new project objective targeting strengthening the country’s capacity to be able to benefit from its WTO membership was agreed upon. To achieve this objective meant that individual and organizational trade policy capacity needed to be enhanced, as well as coordination, consultation and stakeholders’ mechanisms needed to be operational. The individual trade policy capacity building had been fruitful but to a varying degree. The draft report of the ex-post evaluation noted that a core group of 12 to 18 staff (mainly from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MoCI)) had gained an impressive technical trade policy knowledge. A larger group of stakeholders from government, business and civil society with a solid level of awareness also exist and number approximately 40-60 people. Their Knowledge on WTO agreements, legal requirements and WTO negotiations was increased and applied. For enhanced institutional capacity, a Division for Foreign Trade was established at the MoCI and served as a secretariat for coordinating WTO issues, amongst other things. National Inquiry points for Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) at MoCI and Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) measures at Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) were established. Other technical and operational support (office equipment, internet services) were provided and utilized. Civil society, private sector, the Legislature, and other ministries and agencies were identified as the main target groups that needed to be aware of Liberia WTO accession process. As it relates to stakeholders’ engagement, apart from a few specific awareness-raising activities, general outreach to civil society was done indirectly through e.g. media coverage, the MoCI website, radio shows and open seminars. The Liberian legislators and other ministries and agencies were made aware and supported Liberia’s WTO accession. The private sector was made aware, but support was not significant. This intervention supported the launching of a new service portal in July 2018 called the Lib Business Hub (https://www.libbusinesshub.com/). The Business Hub is a web based service portal that provides in one place a wide range of information to foreign and domestic investors and business people on how to start, run and close a business in Liberia. It contains rules, regulations and procedure about doing business in Liberia. The service portal is an initiative that was earmarked as important for the advancement of trade in the Liberia WTO post accession plan, as well as in the World Bank 2008 and 2013 Diagnostic Trade Integrated Study. The Business Hub will contribute to connecting Liberia to the multilateral trading system through access to information on business transactions in Liberia. Overall, the relevance and effectiveness of the contribution was rated very high, management of contribution was rated high and impact rated medium to high, efficiency was rated high on the individual level but low on the institutional level, and sustainability was rated low.
